name: Counting Arrays
description: You are given two positive integer numbers x and y . An array F is called an y -factorization of x iff the following conditions are met: There are y elements in F , and all of them are integer numbers; . You have to count the number of pairwise distinct arrays that are y -factorizations of x . Two arrays A and B are considered different iff there exists at least one index i ( 1 ≤ i ≤ y ) such that A i ≠ B i . Since the answer can be very large, print it modulo 10 9 + 7 .
input_specification: The first line contains one integer q ( 1 ≤ q ≤ 10 5 ) — the number of testcases to solve. Then q lines follow, each containing two integers x i and y i ( 1 ≤ x i , y i ≤ 10 6 ). Each of these lines represents a testcase.
output_specification: Print q integers. i -th integer has to be equal to the number of y i -factorizations of x i modulo 10 9 + 7 .
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
